recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. If a future work-group decision wants mandatory policy fields for specific consent scopes, handle that separately in a profile or implementation guide as FHIR-25387 suggested.
issue_request: FHIR-25387 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Consent. It requested removal of the invariant requiring either Consent.policy or Consent.policyRule, plus guidance that a Consent lacking those discrete elements must still include the policy being agreed to or complied with and that computable policy data should be populated as practical.
initial_application: Commit ef9cfd82f064d240af8c68721cd8be34aa582177, merged by d2ce402b659ea2cec4b59333b27050d9a43f2711, disabled the old policy-exists invariant in source/consent/consent-spreadsheet.xml and added the Jira guidance as a comment on the old Consent.policy row. Later refactoring in 3d15d8f10db9fb3f2f57469a3fa986e3baebc1f0 removed the retired policy/policyRule block and dropped that guidance.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. The current source uses policyBasis and policyText instead of the retired policy and policyRule names, and sourceAttachment/sourceReference instead of source[x]. FHIR-13360 was an earlier no-change request for the same invariant, FHIR-25557 was only a same-commit quote fix, and later Consent refactors such as FHIR-39597 changed naming/model context without reversing FHIR-25387.
reconciliation: Added an ElementDefinition.comment to Consent.policyBasis in source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml restoring the missing guidance with current element names. No invariant was reintroduced.
source_changes: source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml: added a Consent.policyBasis comment that restores fallback policy guidance using policyBasis, policyText, sourceReference, and sourceAttachment.
